questions.question: What uniquely identifies a traditional CloudWatch metric?
options: Namespace, metric name, and the complete set of dimension name/value pairs
Dashboard name and widget color
Alarm name and notification topic
Log group and retention period
questions.explanation: CloudWatch treats each namespace, metric name, and unique dimension combination as a separate metric time series.

questions.question: A metric uses 4 service values, 3 environments, and 8 operations. How many distinct time series can that one metric name create?
questions.explanation: Dimension combinations multiply: 4 x 3 x 8 equals 96 separate time series.

questions.question: Where should a request ID usually be placed?
options: In every metric's dimension set
In structured logs or traces used for request-level investigation
In the metric namespace
In the alarm threshold
questions.explanation: Request IDs are useful for high-cardinality investigation, but using them as metric dimensions creates a separate custom metric for each unique value.

questions.question: What does a 3-out-of-5 alarm rule mean?
options: The metric must publish exactly three values total
At least three of the five evaluated periods must breach
The alarm waits five hours and runs three actions
Three separate metrics must share five dimensions
questions.explanation: DatapointsToAlarm is M and EvaluationPeriods is N. A 3-out-of-5 rule enters ALARM when at least three periods in the evaluated window breach.

questions.question: A failure-count metric publishes only when failures occur. Which missing-data policy commonly matches that sparse contract?
options: Treat missing as not breaching
Treat missing as breaching
Use request IDs as dimensions
Disable alarm actions
questions.explanation: For a deliberately sparse failure metric, no data can mean no failure event. This policy is unsafe for a continuous heartbeat, where silence may indicate broken telemetry.

questions.question: Why should a Logs Insights query use narrow log groups and a short time range?
options: Queries are evaluated only on dashboard data
Query charges depend on uncompressed log data scanned, and a smaller scope also reduces irrelevant results
CloudWatch deletes any log group that is queried broadly
Narrow queries automatically change log retention
questions.explanation: Logs Insights scans selected log data. Constraining groups and time bounds reduces scanned volume and keeps the investigation focused.
